newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WOODS 13 ADRIFT AS CLARKE FORGES ON.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WOODS 13 ADRIFT AS CLARKE FORGES ON.

text.p: Tiger Woods suffered a quadruple-bogey eight in a three-over-par 74 to trail leader Darren Clarke by 13 shots in the second round of the British Open at Royal Troon on Friday.
Woods found to his cost that a Scottish gorse bush is a dangerous obstacle as he struggled to his eight at the 10th hole.
But a birdie at the last from 20 feet guaranteed his place in the weekend field and preserved his hopes that he could still win even from so far back.
Briton Clarke added a five-under 66 to his opening 67 to equal the record 133 for the first 36 holes of an Open at Royal Troon, set by American Bobby Clampett in 1982.
That left him three shots clear of Sweden's 1994 British Open runner-up Jesper Parnevik, also round in 66.
American Jim Furyk, joint overnight leader with Clarke, slipped to six behind the lead with a one-over 72.
Woods, U.S. Msters champion and world number one, was level par after the front nine after two birdies and two three-putt bogeys.
At the 10th his drive finished in rough and his eight-iron from there flew over the green into thick rough with a gorse bush just behind his ball.
Taking a sand wedge he caught the bush on his downswing and moved the ball just a few inches.
"The club went right underneath the ball," he said. He then hacked his fourth just six yards, chipped back past the green with his fifth, chipped up to 12 feet and two-putted.
That setback after a triple-bogey seven at the 11th hole in his first-round 72 left him virtually out of contention.
"If you take away those two holes I could be three-under. I had two bad holes at the wrong times. Other than that I've played well. I've hit the ball very well this week," he said.
"I don't think I'm too far back to win. I was more than that behind at Pebble Beach this year and I almost won.
"Hopefully I can get off to a good start tomorrow. If I can make some birdies, I'll hopefully post a better number."
Clarke, third in the European Ryder Cup standings, continued his fine form with a four-under front nine containing six birdies, two bogeys and just one par.
Three birdies came on putts of around 20 feet and he holed two more from that distance on the back nine.
"I got my momentum early and just kept going," said the Northern Ireland player.
He admitted he was beginning to think about the possibility of winning after saying on Thursday he regarded just getting close as the next step in his career.
"If I can get myself into contention on Sunday afternoon, I do believe I can give it a go," he said.
Parnevik birdied the last three holes of his first round, two with long putts, but changed his putter overnight.
"I didn't feel comfortable all day yesterday on the greens -- or with my game," he said.
The U.S.-based Swede, the only player to break par on the back nine on Thursday, bogeyed the first hole on Friday.
But a three-iron second to six feet set up an eagle three at the fourth. He made four more birdies then saved par from 50 feet with a big-breaking putt at the last.

Defending champion Tom Lehman followed his 74 with a one-over 72 in which he took a triple-bogey seven at the second including a two-shot penalty for not replacing his ball marker in the correct place on the green.
Lehman moved his marker as it was in the line of a playing partner's putt and forgot to move it back when it was his turn to putt.
"That is the first time I have ever done that," he said. "I put it back down and forgot to move it."
U.S. Open champion Ernie Els shot a two-under 69 to get back to two over after his opening 75 while three times champion Nick Faldo carded a 73 to be plus two.
